cards.english: Glad to see you!
cards.existing: Possessives shift too: `твой` (your, informal) vs `ваш` (your, formal/plural). And the cases: `тебя/тебе/тобой` (informal) vs `вас/вам/вами` (formal/plural).

cards.english: My brother runs in the afternoon.
cards.existing: Add prefixes for more nuance: `при-` (arrive), `у-` (leave), `пере-` (cross), `до-` (reach). `Прихожу домой` (I arrive home), `ухожу` (I leave).

cards.english: I like this song.
cards.existing: Past tense agrees with the liked thing too: `Мне нравилась эта песня` (Mne nravilas' eta pesnya) (I liked this song – agrees with song, fem). Gender follows the object.

cards.english: She gave flowers to mom.
He became a famous doctor.
Father read a book recently.
We are proud of our children.
I try not to be late.
We left early in the morning.
Mom read a book in the evening.
The girl read a book in the morning.
Mushroom soup smells wonderful.
cards.existing: Professions in instrumental: `работаю учителем` (rabotayu uchitelem) (I work as a teacher). When you 'become' or 'be' something in professional sense, use instrumental.

cards.english: She practices yoga every morning.
She met an interesting person.
She told about her childhood.
A doctor's work requires great patience.
A sturdy table stands in the corner.
A bright lamp hangs above the table.
We met friends at the train station.
Under the tree there is an old bench.
Behind the fence there is a big garden.

cards.target: Мы гуляем с собакой каждый вечер.
cards.english: We walk with the dog every evening.
cards.existing: Times of day are already instrumental: `утром` (in the morning), `вечером` (in the evening). No preposition – the case carries the meaning.

cards.target: Дети играют с мячом во дворе.
cards.english: Children play with a ball in the yard.

cards.target: Мама обычно помогает другу на рынке.
cards.english: Mom usually helps a friend at the market.

cards.target: Мальчику подарили велосипед на день рождения.
cards.english: The boy was given a bicycle for his birthday.

cards.target: Между работой и домом ехать полчаса.
cards.english: It takes half an hour to travel between work and home.

cards.target: Полицейский всегда пишет отчёты на работе.
cards.english: The policeman always writes reports at work.
Tomorrow the nurse will help a friend.

cards.target: Ребёнок часто помогает другу в парке.
cards.english: A child often helps a friend in the park.

cards.target: Девочка стирала одежду дома на прошлой неделе.
cards.english: The girl did laundry at home last week.

cards.target: Бутерброд с сыром – мой любимый завтрак.
cards.english: A sandwich with cheese is my favorite breakfast.

cards.target: После работы я обычно захожу в магазин.
cards.english: After work I usually stop by the shop.
This morning grandfather is helping a friend.

cards.target: На прошлой неделе брат стирал одежду дома.
cards.english: Last week brother did laundry at home.
Colleagues liked my presentation.
The librarian usually watches a movie.
The boy eats soup with a spoon.
She waved her hand in farewell.
She looks after her younger brother.
A beautiful house stands on the corner.
Students were given a lot of homework.
I am well aware of this problem.
She cuts bread with a sharp knife.
She is satisfied with her new job.
cards.existing: `Свой` (Svoy) agrees with the noun it modifies in gender/number/case, just like other possessives. `Свой дом` (m), `своя машина` (f), `своё окно` (n).

cards.english: He greeted his colleagues in the morning.
She decorated the room with fresh flowers.
The friend sometimes swims in the pool.
An old piano stands in the room.
An old oak grows in front of the house.
The square in front of the theater is very beautiful.
The salesman always does laundry at home.

cards.target: Она всегда включает музыку, когда готовит.
cards.english: She always puts on music while cooking.

cards.target: Мы провели все выходные на даче.
cards.english: We spent the whole weekend at the dacha.

cards.target: Друг обычно покупает продукты в магазине.
cards.english: The friend usually buys groceries in the store.

cards.target: У входа в здание стоит охранник.
cards.english: A guard stands at the entrance to the building.

cards.target: Библиотекарь обычно танцует вальс на вечеринке.
cards.english: The librarian usually dances a waltz at the party.

cards.target: Я начинаю день с чашки крепкого кофе.
cards.english: I start my day with a cup of strong coffee.
After work the teacher helps a friend.

cards.target: Мы ехали поездом из Москвы в Петербург.
cards.english: We traveled by train from Moscow to Petersburg.
cards.existing: Walking vs vehicle: `идти (idti)/ходить` for on foot, `ехать/ездить` for any vehicle. Russian distinguishes how you move, English doesn't.

cards.target: Рада вас видеть после такого долгого перерыва.
cards.english: Glad to see you after such a long break.
The programmer dances a waltz at the party.

cards.target: Друг гулял в парке на прошлой неделе.
cards.english: The friend walked in the park last week.
Mathematics comes easily to her.
He is interested in Russian history.
A lighthouse stands on the seashore.
She speaks with a slight accent.
